opex.note: Marketing the movies, shows and parks, and running the company.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: The wear and tear on parks, cruise ships and equipment, spread over their working lives.

opex.name: Restructuring & impairment charges
opex.note: Costs of reshaping parts of the business and writing down assets that lost value.

follow100Note: Of the $14.40 kept as profit per $100 of revenue, about $0.53 belongs to noncontrolling partners — $13.86 is Disney shareholders'. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Of the $3,401M of net income, $126M belongs to noncontrolling partners; $3,275M is attributable to Disney (the $1.81 EPS figure).

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs a $0.01 loss a year ago

oneTimers: Income taxes were a $314M benefit this quarter rather than an expense — the release does not attribute it to a single item — so reported net income ($3,401M) came in above pre-tax income ($3,087M).
Restructuring and impairment charges were $109M — a fraction of the $2,052M recorded a year ago, which had dragged the year-ago quarter to a small loss for Disney shareholders.
otherDetail: Interest expense, net, of $346M on Disney's debt, partly offset by $36M of equity income from companies Disney part-owns.
segmentNote: Segment operating income: Entertainment $1,258M, Sports $687M, Experiences $2,491M (before corporate costs).

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Streaming subscriptions, TV networks and channels, park tickets and hotel stays — the large majority of Disney's money.

segments.name: Products
segments.note: Merchandise, food and drinks, and other things Disney physically sells.

takeaways.text: Experiences — parks, resorts and cruises — grew operating income to $2,491M, with domestic parks up 13% to $1.8B on higher guest spending and consumer products up 14%.
takeaways.title: Experiences kept growing

takeaways.text: Entertainment operating income rose 61% to $1,258M: Direct-to-Consumer operating income jumped to $336M from $47M, with 180.7 million Disney+ and Hulu subscriptions (126.0 million Disney+). Content sales swung back to profit.
takeaways.title: Streaming profit jumped seven-fold

takeaways.text: Reported net income was $3,401M ($1.81 a share) — helped by a $314M income-tax benefit, which is why net income came in above pre-tax income. Adjusted EPS, excluding such items, was $1.45, up 20%.
takeaways.title: A tax benefit padded the bottom line

verdict: Disney grew revenue 7% to $23.6B and segment profit 15% to $4.4B — parks set the pace and streaming profit jumped — and reported net income swung to $3.4B from a shareholder loss a year ago, when $2.1B of write-downs hit.
